title: Jensen Huang agrees to testify before Congress by Thanksgiving
body:
## Agreement reached

Jensen Huang, the former chief executive of Nvidia, has agreed to testify before Congress by Thanksgiving, according to statements made by Representative Brian Mast, chairman of the House Foreign Affairs Committee, on November 12, 2026. The agreement was reported by TechCrunch, Bloomberg, NBC and CNN on the same day, hours after Huang resigned from Nvidia with immediate effect. The testimony is expected to take place behind closed doors and under oath, although no final date has been set and the arrangement remains tentative.

Mast said the agreement was reached on Wednesday night, hours before the resignation was announced on Thursday. The timing places the testimony within two weeks of the agreement, with Thanksgiving falling on November 26, 2026. Mast added that the appearance could take place as soon as the following week, while emphasising that the date is still being negotiated.

## Committees and scope

The testimony is expected to be heard by three House committees: the House Foreign Affairs Committee, the House Select Committee on the Chinese Communist Party, and the House Permanent Select Committee on Intelligence. The three committees sent a joint letter on November 4, 2026, requesting Huang's appearance. The Foreign Affairs Committee is chaired by Mast, the China panel by Representative John Moolenaar, and the intelligence committee by Representative Rick Crawford.

According to the reporting, the questioning is expected to focus on two subjects. The first is Huang's reported ties to an alleged Chinese intelligence asset, identified in reporting as Alice Huang. The second is Nvidia's internal security protocols, together with the export controls that govern the sale of advanced computing hardware. The allegations concerning Alice Huang have not been substantiated in public reporting, she has not been charged, and Nvidia's board has stated that it found no evidence that information was compromised. This article refers to the matter only as alleged, in line with the available evidence.

Mast has also stated an expectation that the testimony will be video-recorded and transcribed. That expectation has not been confirmed as a settled arrangement, and it should not be read as a final term of the appearance. The under-oath character of the testimony is likewise described as expected rather than confirmed in final form.

## A measured statement from the chairman

Mast addressed the agreement in remarks that acknowledged both his disagreements with Huang and the significance of Nvidia to the United States. His statement was reported verbatim in two sources:

"Jensen and I have been very at odds as some of you already know on export controls, but Nvidia is a very important company to the United States of America. I don't want to see anything hurt in Nvidia, but he has some very serious questions to answer."

The statement indicates that the committee's interest is centred on the questions Huang is expected to answer, rather than on the company itself. Mast's reference to export controls reflects a longstanding area of disagreement between the two men, and one that is directly relevant to the committees' jurisdiction over technology transfers.

## Background: the resignation

The testimony agreement follows a day of rapid change at Nvidia. On November 12, 2026, Huang resigned as chief executive with immediate effect, ending a tenure at the head of the company he co-founded. Nvidia announced that Colette Kress, previously chief financial officer, had been named interim chief executive while retaining the chief financial officer role. Harvey C. Jones was named the company's first board chair.

The resignation and the testimony agreement are distinct events, and neither has been presented by the company or by the committees as a consequence of the other. The agreement to testify was reached on Wednesday night, before the resignation was announced on Thursday. No statement from Nvidia has connected the two developments, and this article draws no such connection.

## Why it matters

The testimony, if it proceeds as described, places the former chief executive of the world's most prominent artificial intelligence hardware company before three congressional committees at a moment of intense scrutiny over the flow of advanced computing technology. Nvidia's graphics processing units are central to the training and deployment of large artificial intelligence models, and the company's export practices have been a recurring subject of congressional attention.

The scope of the questioning, as reported, extends beyond a single individual. The committees are expected to examine Nvidia's security protocols, which determine how the company protects its technology and information, and the export controls that limit the sale of advanced chips to certain destinations. Both subjects bear directly on United States policy toward the global semiconductor supply chain and on the competitive position of American technology companies.

The closed-door format also matters. Testimony behind closed doors allows the committees to address classified or commercially sensitive material that could not be discussed in a public hearing. At the same time, the expectation of a video recording and a transcript, if confirmed, would preserve a record of the proceedings for the committees' further work.

## What is not yet known

Several elements of the arrangement remain unresolved. No final date has been set, and the agreement is described as tentative. The precise format of the testimony, including whether it will be video-recorded and transcribed, has not been confirmed as a settled term. The committees have not published a witness list, a schedule, or a detailed list of topics beyond those reported.

The allegations concerning Alice Huang also remain unproven in public reporting. She has not been charged, and Nvidia's board has stated that it found no evidence that information was compromised. Any reporting that presents the allegations as established fact would exceed the available evidence.

## What happens next

The next step is the negotiation of a final date for the testimony, which Mast has indicated could fall as soon as the week of November 16, 2026. The three committees are expected to confirm the date and format once those discussions conclude. Further reporting is expected to clarify whether the testimony will be recorded and transcribed, and whether any public statement will follow the closed-door session.

The development is a genuine follow-up to two earlier stories: Huang's resignation as Nvidia chief executive on November 12, and the separate reporting that President Donald Trump had suggested Apple chief executive Tim Cook as a possible successor. The testimony agreement is a new development with its own reporting, not a restatement of either story.

Source: TechCrunch, November 12, 2026; Times Now (CNN), November 12, 2026; The Times of India (Bloomberg), November 12, 2026.

title: Intergalactic enters final stage of production — gameplay reveal in 2027
body:
Naughty Dog has confirmed that Intergalactic: The Heretic Prophet, the science fiction action adventure announced in December 2024, has entered the final stage of production. Neil Druckmann, the studio head and the creative director of the game, said the title is now fully playable and that the development team is refining and polishing it. He also confirmed that Naughty Dog will present gameplay footage and additional story material in 2027. No release date has been announced, and no release window has been given.

The update was reported on 12 November 2026 by Video Games Chronicle, GameSpot and ComicBook, drawing on remarks Druckmann made in conversation with the actor and comedian Patton Oswalt at the Comic Creators Block Party 2026. It is the first substantive progress report on the game since its reveal, almost two years after the announcement trailer was shown at The Game Awards on 12 December 2024.

## The Announcement

Druckmann described the current state of the project in direct terms. "But we're kind of at the last stage of production, where we can play it, and we're refining and polishing it, and I can't wait to show it to the world," he said. The statement places the game in the final phase of development, in which the complete experience exists in playable form and the remaining work consists of iteration, balance and polish rather than the construction of new systems or content.

Druckmann was equally direct about the timing of the next public showing. "We're going to show a lot next year… We're going to show gameplay, more of the story," he said. In a separate remark reported by GameSpot, he added: "In 2027, that changes. We'll fully reveal Intergalactic: The Heretic Prophet." The two statements together establish that the gameplay reveal will take place in 2027, while the precise date of that reveal remains undisclosed.

The remarks do not include a release date. No statement from Naughty Dog or from Sony Interactive Entertainment, the publisher, has attached a year or a window to the launch of the game. Any report that assigns a 2027 release date to the title would go beyond what has been confirmed.

## What Druckmann Said

Beyond the production update, Druckmann offered a measured indication of the direction of the game. "I think we're going to really surprise people with what they think the game is and what it actually is," he said. The comment suggests that the public understanding of the title, formed from the single reveal trailer, does not capture the full scope of the finished game, although Druckmann did not specify the nature of the difference.

He also characterised the design of the game as a synthesis of the studio's earlier work. "It really is a combination of those three franchises [Uncharted, The Last of Us, Jak and Daxter], and we really wanted to expand our deep gameplay systems," he said. The reference covers three distinct traditions within Naughty Dog: the cinematic action adventure of Uncharted, the survival and narrative focus of The Last of Us, and the platforming and world design of Jak and Daxter. The stated ambition is to combine those elements while extending the depth of the gameplay systems, a claim that will be tested when gameplay footage is shown in 2027.

## The Game So Far

Intergalactic: The Heretic Prophet was first revealed at The Game Awards on 12 December 2024. The announcement trailer introduced the protagonist, Jordan A. Mun, played by the actor Tati Gabrielle. Jordan is a bounty hunter who becomes stranded on Sempiria, a distant planet that has been cut off from outside contact for centuries. The trailer presented a retro-futuristic science fiction setting, with 1980s-inspired design, analogue technology and a soundtrack built around the music of the Pet Shop Boys and Nine Inch Nails.

The setting carries a specific narrative premise. Sempiria is a planet from which no one has been heard in more than 600 years, according to the material released at the reveal. Jordan travels there in pursuit of a bounty, and her ship is damaged on arrival, leaving her stranded. The premise establishes isolation as a central condition of the story, a theme that has also shaped the studio's previous work.

The game is being developed for PlayStation 5. It is the first new intellectual property from Naughty Dog since The Last of Us in 2013, and the first game directed by Druckmann since The Last of Us Part II in 2020. The studio has released no further trailer since the reveal, and no gameplay footage has been shown in public. The absence of new material over nearly two years had led to speculation about the state of the project, speculation that the latest remarks address directly.

## Why It Matters

The confirmation that the game is playable and in the final stage of production resolves the principal uncertainty that has surrounded the project since its reveal. A game that has reached this stage has passed through pre-production, full production and content completion, and the remaining work is concerned with quality rather than with the existence of the game itself.

The timing also matters for Sony Interactive Entertainment. The PlayStation 5 platform has relied heavily on established franchises in recent years, and a new intellectual property from the studio responsible for two of the most acclaimed series on the platform carries considerable weight. The 2027 gameplay reveal will be the first opportunity for the public to assess whether the combination of influences described by Druckmann produces a distinct experience.

The measured tone of the announcement is also significant. Druckmann did not promise a release date, did not describe specific gameplay systems in detail, and did not characterise the 2027 showing beyond gameplay and story material. The restraint is consistent with a project that is still in refinement, and it leaves the studio room to set expectations when the footage is ready.

## What Comes Next

The next confirmed milestone is the gameplay reveal in 2027. No event has been named, and no month has been specified. The Game Awards, which takes place in December, is the venue at which the game was first revealed, and PlayStation has also used its own State of Play broadcasts for major showings, but no source has linked the reveal to a specific event.

Until that showing, the public record on the game consists of the reveal trailer, the casting of Tati Gabrielle as Jordan A. Mun, the Sempiria setting, and the remarks reported on 12 November 2026. The production update confirms that the project is advancing on schedule toward a public showing, and that the showing will include the first gameplay footage and a fuller account of the story.

Source: Video Games Chronicle / GameSpot / ComicBook, 12 November 2026.

title: Trump says Tim Cook should replace Jensen Huang as Nvidia CEO
body:
United States President Donald Trump has publicly suggested that Tim Cook, the former chief executive of Apple, should succeed Jensen Huang as chief executive of Nvidia. The suggestion was made in a post on Truth Social on Thursday, hours after Huang resigned from the chipmaker. The post carries no formal authority over the appointment, and no evidence has emerged that Nvidia has approached Cook or that Cook has any interest in the position.

## The Suggestion

In the Truth Social post, Trump wrote that Huang had done a fantastic job and that, now that he had resigned, there was only one man to take his place: Tim Cook of Apple. The post concluded with the sentence, "A Legend replaces a Legend!"

The statement was framed as a personal recommendation from the president. It did not cite any discussion with Nvidia, with its board of directors, or with Cook. No accompanying statement from the White House elaborated on the post, and no official channel has indicated that the suggestion reflects a formal process of any kind.

## The Resignation

Huang resigned on Thursday as president, chief executive officer and member of the board of Nvidia, effective immediately. The resignation ended a tenure of 33 years at the company he co-founded in 1993. Under his leadership, Nvidia grew from a graphics processor company into the most valuable supplier of the accelerators that power large-scale artificial intelligence systems.

Nvidia announced the transition in an official release on Thursday. The company did not state a reason for the resignation in the announcement, and the statement did not address the reports that had circulated in preceding days about pressure on Huang. Reporting by The Wall Street Journal and The New York Times had described an investigation by the board and allegations concerning Huang, but those reports remain attributed claims rather than established findings. Reuters has reported that it could not independently verify the allegations.

## The Interim Leadership

Nvidia named Colette Kress, the chief financial officer, as interim chief executive officer. The company also named Harvey C. Jones as its first board chair, a newly created role. The appointments were announced in the same release that confirmed the resignation.

Kress has served as chief financial officer since 2013 and is among the longest-serving members of the senior leadership team. Her appointment as interim chief executive provides continuity while the board conducts a search for a permanent successor. The company has stated that the board will consider internal and external candidates.

## Cook's Position at Apple

Cook stepped down as chief executive of Apple in September 2026, when John Ternus succeeded him. Cook remains at Apple as executive chairman, a role that keeps him involved in the company's governance while day-to-day operations rest with his successor.

Cook led Apple for fifteen years, from 2011 to 2026. During that period, the company expanded its services business, entered new product categories including wearable devices and spatial computing, and maintained its position among the most valuable public companies in the world. Cook has not commented publicly on Trump's suggestion, and no statement from Apple has addressed it.

## A Reversal in Tone

Trump's suggestion represents a sharp change in his public position on Huang. Days earlier, on 8 and 9 November, the president had publicly defended Huang, describing him as a fine person and an honorable guy and stating that he should remain in his position. The defence came as reports of board scrutiny of Huang were circulating.

The reversal is the second notable shift in the sequence of events. On 10 November, prominent technology figures including Elon Musk and Tim Sweeney publicly urged Nvidia's board to retain Huang. Two days later, Huang resigned, and the president who had defended him then proposed his replacement.

## Why It Matters

The suggestion matters because of the scale of the company involved. Nvidia supplies the majority of the accelerators used to train and operate large artificial intelligence models, and its market value has made it one of the most closely watched companies in the world. A change of chief executive at the company is a matter of direct interest to investors, to customers in the technology industry, and to policymakers who regard advanced semiconductors as a strategic asset.

The suggestion also matters because of the identity of the proposed successor. Cook is one of the most experienced operating executives in the technology industry, and his record at Apple is widely regarded as a standard for supply-chain management and operational discipline. A move from Apple to Nvidia would be one of the most consequential executive transitions in the history of the technology sector.

At the same time, the suggestion has no standing in the appointment process. The selection of a chief executive is a decision of the board of directors, and Nvidia has given no indication that it has approached Cook or that Cook would accept such a role. The distinction between a public suggestion and a formal candidacy is central to the reporting of this development.

## What Happens Next

Nvidia's board will now conduct a search for a permanent chief executive. The company has stated that it will consider internal and external candidates, and the appointment of an interim chief executive and a first board chair indicates that the board intends to manage the transition in an orderly manner.

Three questions will determine the course of the search. The first is whether the board looks inside the company, where senior executives with direct experience of the accelerator business are available, or outside it, where a candidate of Cook's profile would be considered. The second is whether Cook responds to the suggestion at all, since his silence to date leaves the proposal without a counterpart. The third is whether the president returns to the subject, since further public comment could alter the pressure on the board even without any formal authority over the decision.

Until those questions are answered, the suggestion remains what it was when it was posted: a public recommendation by the president of the United States, not a decision by the board of Nvidia, not an appointment, and not a confirmed candidacy.

Source: The Wall Street Journal live coverage; Al Jazeera liveblog; New Straits Times (AFP wire); NDTV; official Nvidia announcement, 12 November 2026.

title: Samsung reveals Intelligent Eyewear prices — pre-orders open now
body:
Samsung has opened pre-orders for its Intelligent Eyewear in the United States and South Korea, disclosing official prices for the first time and confirming that shipments will begin on December 10, 2026. The announcement, published by Samsung Mobile Press on November 12, 2026, converts a product that was previously presented without pricing into a purchasable device with a defined launch date.

The eyewear is developed in partnership with Google, with Google Gemini built into the device. Samsung is offering the product in two eyewear collections, produced with Gentle Monster and Warby Parker, and the total range comprises 30 designs.

## Pre-order window and availability

Pre-orders opened on November 12, 2026, in the United States and South Korea. The pre-order period closes on December 10, 2026, the same date on which shipments and the formal launch are scheduled to begin.

The full lineup is available in the United States. In South Korea, only the Gentle Monster collection is offered. Samsung has stated that additional markets will follow next year, although the company did not disclose which markets or a timetable for them at the time of the announcement.

## Pricing by market and model

In the United States, the Warby Parker collection starts at 395 dollars. The Gentle Monster collection is priced from 449 dollars to 489 dollars, with the exact price depending on the model selected. In South Korea, the Gentle Monster collection starts at 650,000 won.

The distinction between a starting price and a price range is material to the announcement. The Warby Parker figure is a floor, not a fixed price for every model, and the Gentle Monster figure is a range across its variants. A buyer selecting a specific frame and lens combination should therefore expect the final price to depend on that configuration.

## The two collections

The 30 designs are divided between the two partners. The Gentle Monster collection contains 16 variants across six frame designs. The Warby Parker collection contains 14 variants across three frame designs.

The two collections therefore address different segments of the market. Gentle Monster contributes the larger share of variants and frame designs, while Warby Parker offers a smaller set of frames at a lower starting price. The company has not disclosed how individual variants are distributed across the two price bands within the Gentle Monster range.

## Hardware specification

The eyewear is powered by the Snapdragon AR1 Gen 1 processor. It carries a 12 megapixel high dynamic range camera, 2 gigabytes of memory and 64 gigabytes of storage. Audio is delivered through open-ear speakers, and the device includes four microphones.

The device weighs approximately 41 grams, although weight varies by model. Battery life is rated at up to nine hours of use, extending to up to 72 hours with the charging case. Both figures are stated as maximums under mixed use, and the company did not publish a figure for continuous use under a single workload. The device is rated IPX4, which denotes resistance to water splashes.

## Software and the Google partnership

Google Gemini is built into the eyewear, and the product was developed with Google. The announcement does not describe the precise division of responsibilities between the two companies, and it does not state which version of the underlying platform software the device runs. Prior coverage has associated the product with Google smart glasses work, but the press release itself does not present a platform name as a fact, and this article does not assert one on its behalf.

## Background

This announcement is a genuine follow-up to Newzora content 28, published on November 11, 2026, which reported that Samsung and Google smart glasses pre-orders would open on Thursday, November 12. At that stage, no official pricing had been disclosed. The November 12 announcement supplies the missing information: firm prices for both collections, the confirmed December 10 ship date, and the detailed specification of the device.

The timing places Samsung in a segment that has attracted sustained attention from large technology companies. Smart glasses that combine a camera, voice assistance and an open-ear audio design have moved from demonstration hardware toward commercial products over the past two years, and the involvement of Google as a software partner gives this device a direct connection to one of the largest artificial intelligence platforms in the market.

## Why the announcement matters

The pricing is the most significant element of the announcement. A starting price of 395 dollars for the Warby Parker collection positions the device below the price of a flagship smartphone, while the Gentle Monster range of 449 to 489 dollars places the premium variants in the same band as high-end wireless audio and wearable products. The pricing suggests that Samsung is treating the eyewear as a consumer accessory rather than a specialist device.

The December 10 launch date is also significant. It places the product in the market before the end of the year, in time for the holiday purchasing period, and it gives Samsung a defined window in which to measure demand before deciding on the additional markets scheduled for next year.

The specification is comparatively modest in one respect and ambitious in another. The 2 gigabytes of memory and 64 gigabytes of storage are limited by smartphone standards, which is consistent with a device designed to operate as a companion to a phone rather than as a standalone computer. The 12 megapixel camera, the four-microphone array and the nine-hour battery figure, by contrast, indicate that the device is intended for sustained daily use rather than short demonstrations.

## What happens next

The immediate question is the rate at which pre-orders convert into shipments after December 10. Samsung has not disclosed pre-order volumes, and it has not stated whether supply will be constrained at launch. The second question is the timetable for additional markets, which the company has not yet specified. A third question concerns the software experience in daily use, which cannot be assessed until review units reach independent testers.

For prospective buyers, the practical choice is between the two collections. The Warby Parker range offers the lower entry price, while the Gentle Monster range offers more frame designs at a higher price. In South Korea, that choice does not arise, because only the Gentle Monster collection is available.

Source: Samsung Mobile Press official release, SamMobile, The Korea Times, all November 12, 2026.

title: OPPO confirms Reno 17 chips ahead of November 16 launch
body:
## Lede

OPPO has confirmed the processors that will power its Reno 17 series, removing the last major uncertainty about the handsets ahead of their formal launch in China on November 16, 2026. The standard Reno 17 will run on Qualcomm's Snapdragon 7 Gen 4, while the Reno 17 Pro will use MediaTek's Dimensity 8550 Super, according to official teasers published by OPPO on November 12, 2026. The announcement also confirmed a new in-house touch chip, a proprietary communication chip, and the software platform that will ship on both devices.

## What Happened

OPPO published the confirmations through its official Weibo account on November 12, 2026, four days before the launch event scheduled for 7:00 PM CST on November 16. The teasers confirmed the two chipsets and provided the first official detail on the series' supporting silicon. Pre-orders for the handsets are already open in China, according to multiple reports citing OPPO's store listings.

The standard Reno 17 will be powered by the Snapdragon 7 Gen 4, Qualcomm's upper-midrange chipset. The Reno 17 Pro will use the MediaTek Dimensity 8550 Super, a newly branded variant of MediaTek's Dimensity 8550 platform. Both handsets will also carry two OPPO-developed chips: the Lingxi touch chip, which governs touch response, and the Shanhai N1 communication chip, which handles connectivity.

## Performance and Gaming

OPPO's teasers provided the clearest performance detail yet for the series, with an important distinction between the two models. The standard Reno 17 supports gaming at up to 120 frames per second, a figure OPPO confirmed for that model specifically. The Reno 17 Pro, meanwhile, is equipped with a 1.5K native-resolution gaming engine. The two capabilities should not be conflated: the 120fps figure applies to the standard model, while the 1.5K gaming engine is a feature of the Pro.

Both handsets will ship with ColorOS 17, OPPO's latest software platform, which is based on Android 17. OPPO has stated that the series will deliver up to six years of smooth performance, a claim the company has made in its own promotional material and which has not been independently verified. The software also introduces Fluid Cloud, a live-update feature that OPPO previewed in its teasers, which surfaces live activity information on the handset.

## Design and Colours

The series introduces a distinctive finish named "Encounter Cat," a light-blue treatment in which a three-dimensional outline of a cat is embossed on the rear glass panel. The design has been confirmed in OPPO's official imagery for both models.

The standard Reno 17 will be available in three colours: Encounter Cat, Ice Moon White, and Cocoa Brown. The Reno 17 Pro will also be offered in three colours: Encounter Cat, First Snow White, and Cocoa Brown. The two models therefore share two colour options, with the standard model using Ice Moon White and the Pro using First Snow White as their respective light alternatives.

## Cameras

Camera specifications for the Reno 17 Pro have been reported by a single source and should be treated accordingly. As reported by My Mobile India, citing a post on X and OPPO's own teasers, the Reno 17 Pro is expected to carry a 200-megapixel Samsung HP5 main sensor with a 1/1.56-inch sensor size, accompanied by 50-megapixel sensors and support for 4K video recording at 60 frames per second across focal lengths. This information has not been independently confirmed by a second outlet, and it is presented here with that attribution.

Camera specifications for the standard Reno 17 have not yet been revealed, and no official detail on its imaging hardware has been published as of November 12, 2026.

## The Launch Event

The launch event on November 16, 2026, will cover more than the two handsets. OPPO will also introduce the Pad Air 6 tablet and the Watch 5 smartwatch at the same event. The Pad Air 6 is confirmed to feature a 2.8K display with a 120Hz refresh rate, a 10,050mAh battery, and ColorOS 17. The Watch 5 is confirmed to use a square dial with a rotating crown.

Reports on the Watch 5's battery life differ. Gadgets360 reported on November 12 that the watch would offer up to 10 days of battery life, or three days with the always-on display enabled, while an earlier report from Unbox published on November 9 cited up to seven days. Given the discrepancy between sources, no single battery figure for the Watch 5 is stated here.

## What Remains Unconfirmed

Several specifications circulating in advance of the launch remain unconfirmed and must not be treated as fact. No prices have been confirmed for either handset, and no global or India launch date has been announced. The Pro model may not be released in India, while the standard model has been tipped for an India launch in early 2027; that timing is a tip rather than a confirmed plan.

Battery capacities attributed to the handsets, reported as 8,000mAh for the Reno 17 and 7,200mAh for the Reno 17 Pro, remain leak-only and have not been confirmed by OPPO. Display sizes of approximately 6.59 inches for the standard model and approximately 6.32 inches for the Pro are likewise drawn from leaks rather than official sources. Memory configurations that have appeared in store listings are also unconfirmed by the company. The launch on November 16 is confirmed for China only.

## Why It Matters

The Reno series occupies a strategically important position in OPPO's portfolio, sitting between the company's mass-market A series and its flagship Find series. The chipset split between the two models is notable: the standard model receives a Qualcomm platform while the Pro receives a MediaTek platform, a division that allows OPPO to differentiate the two handsets on performance while keeping both within the upper-midrange segment.

The inclusion of OPPO's own Lingxi touch chip and Shanhai N1 communication chip is equally significant. It signals the company's continued investment in proprietary silicon alongside its use of third-party processors, a strategy that has become common among major Chinese manufacturers seeking greater control over the user experience in touch response and connectivity.

The timing of the launch also matters. With the event scheduled for mid-November, the Reno 17 series will enter the Chinese market ahead of the year-end shopping period, giving OPPO a fresh mid-range offering at a moment when competitors are also refreshing their lineups.

## What's Next

The formal launch takes place on November 16, 2026, at 7:00 PM CST in China. That event is expected to confirm the specifications that remain unverified, including the camera details for the standard model, battery capacities, display sizes, memory configurations, and, most importantly, pricing. Any India launch, which has been tipped for the standard model in early 2027, is likely to be announced only after the China launch has taken place. Until then, the confirmed facts are the chipsets, the in-house touch and communication chips, the ColorOS 17 software platform, the Encounter Cat design, and the launch date.

Source: Gadgets360 / Beebom

title: Jensen Huang resigns as Nvidia CEO
body:
Nvidia announced on Thursday, 12 November 2026, that Jensen Huang has resigned as president, chief executive officer and member of the board of directors, effective immediately. The announcement ends a period of leadership that lasted 33 years, from the founding of the company in 1993 to the present day. The board of directors accepted the resignation on Wednesday, 11 November, according to a regulatory filing cited by Reuters.

The company did not give a reason for the departure in its announcement. Nvidia thanked Huang for his contributions over 33 years and said nothing further about the circumstances of the decision. The statement also did not address the allegations reported in recent days by The Wall Street Journal and The New York Times.

## The announcement

The announcement was issued by Nvidia through GlobeNewswire on 12 November 2026 at 13:48 UTC under the heading "NVIDIA Announces CEO Transition". It stated that Huang had resigned from all three of his roles at the company: president, chief executive officer and director. The resignation took effect immediately upon announcement.

The board accepted the resignation on Wednesday, 11 November, according to a regulatory filing. The timing places the decision one day before the public announcement, and the filing provides the formal record of the board action. No further detail about the board deliberations has been disclosed.

Huang co-founded Nvidia in 1993 and led the company through its transformation from a graphics processor maker into the dominant supplier of the accelerators that power modern artificial intelligence systems. At 63 years of age, he remained the public face of the company and one of its largest individual shareholders. According to the most recent disclosures, Huang holds approximately 3.61 percent of Nvidia shares, which makes him the fourth-largest investor in the company.

## Interim leadership

Colette Kress, the chief financial officer of Nvidia, has been appointed interim chief executive officer. Kress retains her role as chief financial officer while she serves in the interim position. The board has begun a search for a permanent successor and is considering internal and external candidates, according to the announcement.

Harvey C. Jones has been appointed chair of the board, the first person to hold the title of board chair in the history of the company. Jones is a former chief executive officer of Synopsys and has served as a member of the Nvidia board since 1993, the year the company was founded.

Jones said the board has "full confidence in Colette and the leadership team" and expects "operations, customer commitments and product roadmap to continue without interruption". The statement is the only substantive assurance the company has offered about continuity in the transition period.

## Market reaction

Nvidia shares fell by more than 11 percent in premarket trading on Thursday, 12 November, according to TechCrunch. The shares closed at 173.73 United States dollars on Wednesday, 11 November. The decline extends a sharp slide that began earlier in the week: the company has lost more than 300 billion United States dollars in market value since Friday, and the share price now stands approximately 35 percent below its record close on 6 October 2026.

The scale of the market reaction reflects the centrality of Huang to the investment case for Nvidia. Under his leadership, the company became the most valuable supplier of the hardware on which the current generation of artificial intelligence models is trained and run. Investors now face a period of uncertainty about who will lead the company through the next phase of that market, and about whether the transition will affect product timing or customer relationships.

## Background

Nvidia was founded in 1993 by Huang, Curtis Priem and Chris Malachowsky. The company first built its business on graphics processing units for personal computers and video games, and later found that the same parallel computing architecture was suited to the training of large artificial intelligence models. That second application drove a decade of growth that made Nvidia one of the most valuable companies in the world by market capitalisation.

Huang became known for his direct style of leadership and for his annual keynote presentations, in which he set out the company product roadmap in detail. His tenure is unusual in the technology industry for its length: 33 years as chief executive of a single company, from founding to resignation, is a record matched by few leaders of comparable companies.

## Reported context

The Wall Street Journal and The New York Times have reported allegations concerning Huang in the days preceding the resignation. The details of those reports have not been confirmed by Nvidia, and the company statement gave no reason for the departure and did not address the allegations. Beijing has denied that Alice Huang is a spy, according to the reporting. Reuters has stated that it could not independently verify the allegations or the board plans described in the reporting. The allegations remain unproven claims in published reporting, and they should not be treated as established fact.

## Why it matters

The resignation removes, with immediate effect, the chief executive who has directed Nvidia strategy since its founding. The company now enters a transition at a moment when demand for artificial intelligence accelerators is the central question in the technology industry, and when competitors are seeking to close the gap with Nvidia in hardware and software.

The appointment of an interim chief executive from within the existing leadership, and the appointment of a long-serving board member as chair, suggests that the board intends to signal stability. Jones has served on the board since 1993 and knows the company as well as any outside director can. Kress, as chief financial officer, has direct knowledge of the company financial position and of its customer commitments.

The market reaction, however, shows that investors are not yet satisfied that continuity is assured. A decline of more than 11 percent in premarket trading, following a loss of more than 300 billion United States dollars in market value since Friday, indicates that the market is pricing in a period of uncertainty about leadership, strategy and the timing of future products.

## What happens next

Nvidia is scheduled to report results for the third quarter of fiscal year 2027 on Tuesday, 17 November. The results are expected at approximately 1:20 p.m. Pacific Time, with an earnings call at 2:00 p.m. Pacific Time. The report and the call will be the first formal opportunity for the interim leadership to address investors, and the market will watch closely for any statement about the search for a permanent chief executive, about the product roadmap and about customer demand.

The board search for a permanent successor is now the central question for the company. The announcement states that internal and external candidates are under consideration. No timetable for the appointment has been given.

Source: Reuters; TechCrunch; 9to5Mac; official Nvidia GlobeNewswire release "NVIDIA Announces CEO Transition", 12 November 2026.

title: Musk and Sweeney tell Nvidia's board: save Jensen
body:
Two of the most prominent figures in the technology industry intervened publicly on 12 November 2026 in the deliberations of Nvidia's board of directors over the future of Jensen Huang, the company's co-founder and chief executive. Tim Sweeney, the chief executive of Epic Games, and Elon Musk, the chief executive of Tesla and SpaceX, each posted on X in support of Huang on the day after the board met to discuss his position. Their interventions arrived as the board weighed a decision that, according to reporting by The Wall Street Journal, could end the tenure of the executive most closely associated with the company's rise.

The board met on Wednesday, 11 November, to discuss Huang's future. The Wall Street Journal, citing people familiar with the matter, reported that the board was preparing to oust Huang. No decision has been announced. The Times of India and Outlook India, reporting on 12 November, each state that the board has not announced a decision. Nvidia's shares fell by approximately 8 percent in extended trading on 11 November, according to reports. Reuters has stated that it could not independently verify the affair allegations against Huang or the board's plans.

## The statements

Sweeney posted on X on 12 November. His post reads in full: "Save Jensen. This would be an Apple firing Steve Jobs level of idiocy from NVIDIA's board if they did that, and a grievous harm to the United States of America. The dude truly is the visionary driver of the future of tech from the gaming GPU era to CUDA to AI supercomputers."

Musk's intervention took a different form. He replied to a post by ZeroHedge that read "Elon please hire Jensen". Musk's reply read: "That would be an honor." The exchange was a reply to a post on X, not a job offer. No role was named, no terms were stated, and no hiring process has been reported. Any reading of the reply as an offer of employment would go beyond what Musk wrote.

The comparison Sweeney drew was to the departure of Steve Jobs from Apple in 1985, a removal that is widely regarded as one of the most consequential board decisions in the history of the technology industry. Jobs returned to Apple in 1997. The comparison frames Huang's possible removal as a decision of comparable scale, and it places the weight of the argument on Huang's record rather than on the circumstances that brought the board to consider his position.

## Background

The board's deliberations follow a sequence of events that began on 8 November, when Huang acknowledged infidelity in a letter to Nvidia staff. The board opened an independent investigation, stating that it had "no reason to believe" that national security or Nvidia's secrets were compromised.

On 10 November, the independent directors retained Joon H. Kim, a former acting United States Attorney, to lead the investigation. Kim is a partner at the law firm Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen and Katz. The appointment placed the inquiry in the hands of an external investigator with experience in federal prosecution.

On 11 November, two reports advanced the story in the same day. The New York Times reported on the relationship with Kimberly Powell, and The Wall Street Journal reported that the board was preparing to oust Huang. The shares fell in extended trading after the reports, according to reports of the market reaction.

## The reported reasons

The Wall Street Journal has reported that the board's deliberations concern two extramarital affairs. According to the Journal, one involved Alice Huang, a woman whom United States intelligence suspects of spying for China, and one involved Kimberly Powell, Nvidia's vice president of healthcare and a direct report of Huang.

These details are reported claims, not established facts. The board has not confirmed them, and Reuters has stated that it could not independently verify the affair allegations or the board's plans. The distinction matters, because the board's stated position is that it has no reason to believe that national security or Nvidia's secrets were compromised, while the reported reasons for its deliberations concern personal conduct and the relationships involved. Until the independent investigation led by Kim reports, or the board announces a decision, the reasons for the deliberations remain a matter of reporting rather than of record.

## Why it matters

Huang has led Nvidia since co-founding the company in 1993. Under his leadership, the company moved from graphics processors for gaming into the parallel computing platform CUDA and then into artificial intelligence supercomputers, a transition that placed Nvidia at the centre of the current expansion in artificial intelligence infrastructure. Sweeney's post traces exactly that arc, from the gaming GPU era through CUDA to AI supercomputers, and presents it as the reason the board should retain Huang.

The market reaction on 11 November gives a measure of how investors view the uncertainty. A fall of approximately 8 percent in extended trading followed the reports that the board was preparing to remove the chief executive. The decline reflects the assessment that Huang's leadership is closely tied to the company's valuation, and that a change at the top would introduce risk into a company whose products underpin much of the artificial intelligence industry.

The public interventions by Sweeney and Musk add a further dimension. Both are chief executives of major technology companies, and both chose to address the board directly through public posts rather than through private channels. Their statements do not bind the board, which is responsible to Nvidia's shareholders, but they signal how the wider industry would judge a decision to remove Huang.

## What happens next

No decision has been announced, and the board has not set a public timetable. The independent investigation led by Joon H. Kim is ongoing. Any decision by the board, whether to retain Huang, to remove him, or to take another course, will be announced by the company, and the terms of any such decision will be stated in that announcement.

The reporting will continue as the investigation proceeds. Until then, the facts established on the record are limited: the board met on 11 November, the board has opened an independent investigation, the investigation is led by Kim, no decision has been announced, and two prominent technology chief executives have publicly urged the board to retain Huang.

Source: Times of India, 12 November 2026; Outlook India; The Wall Street Journal; Reuters.

title: GitHub 'wfx-loot' secret stealer hits 61,764 repositories
body:
A campaign that began on 10 November 2026 has turned thousands of hijacked GitHub accounts into a mechanism for stealing secrets from software projects at scale. The campaign, tracked by the security firm Aikido under the name "wfx-loot", used compromised accounts to open probe pull requests across tens of thousands of repositories. Where a probe pull request was merged, a payload ran inside the repository's continuous integration environment and exfiltrated credentials, tokens and files to servers controlled by the attacker. According to Aikido, the payload ran in at least 1,806 repositories, and the campaign was still ongoing on 12 November.

The figures require careful reading, because different numbers describe different parts of the campaign. Aikido reports that 4,837 hijacked GitHub accounts opened probe pull requests in 61,764 repositories. The probe requests carried a consistent signature: the title "docs: dependency audit notes", from branches named "wfx-docs". Between 12:45 UTC on 10 November and 15:00 UTC on 11 November, Aikido counted 61,839 such pull requests. A fourth wave began at 01:00 UTC on 12 November and was still running at 09:08 UTC that day. At that point, 92 percent of the probe pull requests remained open.

## The scale of the campaign

The 61,764 repositories are the repositories that received a probe pull request. The 61,839 pull requests are the number of probe requests opened in the first two waves. The figure for repositories where the payload actually ran is smaller: at least 1,806, according to Aikido. The payload runs only when a probe pull request is merged and the repository's workflow executes, so far fewer repositories saw the payload run than received a request.

One further figure requires a note. Aikido's own reporting gives two numbers for the repositories where the payload ran: a summary figure of 1,835 and a figure of 1,806 in the body of its report. This article uses 1,806, the figure stated in the body of the report, as a lower bound. The discrepancy has not been explained, and the true number may be higher, since the campaign was still running when the report was published. A separate count from Cycode recorded 64,614 probe pull requests in public repositories as of 09:08 UTC on 12 November. That figure counts pull requests, not repositories, and covers public repositories only.

## How the attack works

The attack began at approximately 12:45 UTC on 10 November 2026. Compromised GitHub accounts opened pull requests titled "docs: dependency audit notes" from branches named "wfx-docs". The pull requests were probes: merging one caused the repository's continuous integration workflow to run code supplied by the attacker. The payload executed inside the GitHub Actions runner, the environment in which a repository's automated checks and builds run.

The first waves ran from 12:45 UTC on 10 November to 15:00 UTC on 11 November, producing 61,839 probe pull requests. A fourth wave began at 01:00 UTC on 12 November and continued past 09:08 UTC. With 92 percent of the probe pull requests still open, each one remains a live opportunity for a maintainer to merge it and trigger the payload.

## What the payload steals

The payload targets the secrets that a continuous integration environment holds. According to Aikido, it collects GitHub Actions secrets and variables, the GITHUB_TOKEN issued to the workflow, and OpenID Connect and Actions runtime tokens. It also collects cloud credentials for Amazon Web Services, Microsoft Azure and Google Cloud Platform, and tokens for artificial intelligence tools, including OpenAI, Anthropic, Cursor, Copilot, Gemini and Hugging Face.

The payload also reads credential files, shell histories, files with the .env and .pem extensions, and the memory of processes running on the runner. A single merged pull request can therefore expose credentials for other services as well as the repository itself.

Stolen data was exfiltrated over HTTP POST requests to two addresses: 194.150.166.244 on port 8080, at the path /exfil, and 18.143.168.96 on port 8080, at the same path. A variant that exfiltrates data through Telegram appeared at approximately 05:30 UTC on 12 November, which indicates that the operation was being adapted while it ran.

## Spread into packages

The campaign also spread beyond pull requests into published software packages. The Packagist package digitalelvis/neuronai-studio, version 3.14.3, was found to contain the payload. Any machine that installed that version should be treated as compromised, and its credentials should be treated as exposed.

A Go module was also affected: github.com/onuragtas/docker-env, versions v1.0.278 and v1.0.280. In this case the payload was present only in a workflow file. The Go source code and the compiled binaries were unchanged, and Go builds do not execute workflow files, so installing the module did not run the payload. A compromised workflow file in a package is a risk to the package's own continuous integration environment, not to every user who installs the package, and the two cases should not be described in the same terms.

## Attribution and the GhostAction question

The campaign follows an earlier incident in October 2026, known as GhostAction, in which a similar technique was used to steal secrets through pull requests. Aikido assesses that "wfx-loot" is likely the work of a different actor. The assessment rests on differences in infrastructure, tooling and tradecraft between the two campaigns. The accounts hit by the two campaigns overlap, but Aikido treats that overlap as consistent with the reuse of previously compromised accounts rather than as evidence of a single actor.

No official statement from GitHub has been published on the campaign at the time of writing. Any claim that GitHub has responded should be treated as unverified until such a statement appears.

## Why it matters

The incident matters for three reasons. First, the pull request workflow, the normal mechanism by which open source projects accept contributions, can be turned into a delivery channel for credential theft at scale: a single click by a maintainer can expose an entire set of secrets. Second, the payload targets the credentials that connect a repository to the rest of a developer's infrastructure, so the compromise of one repository can become the compromise of the services around it. Third, the campaign was still running when it was reported, with a fourth wave in progress and the large majority of probe pull requests still open.

## What happens next

The immediate step for maintainers is to check whether any pull request titled "docs: dependency audit notes" from a "wfx-docs" branch has been merged into their repositories, and to treat any merged request as a compromise. Credentials that could have been exposed, including GitHub Actions secrets, cloud credentials and tokens for artificial intelligence tools, should be rotated. Machines that installed digitalelvis/neuronai-studio version 3.14.3 should be treated as compromised.

The wider question is how the platform and the open source community respond to a technique used in two large campaigns within weeks. Aikido's assessment that the two campaigns were run by different actors suggests that the technique itself, rather than a single group, is the problem. Until the pull request workflow is better protected against this form of abuse, the same pattern is likely to appear again.

Source: Aikido blog, 12 November 2026; The Hacker News; Help Net Security; Cycode.

title: IBM unveils Quantum Nighthawk r3 — 1,040-qubit system planned for 2027
body:
IBM announced on 11 November 2026 that it has designed a new quantum processor, the Quantum Nighthawk r3, with 520 programmable qubits, and that it plans to link two such processors into a single 1,040-qubit system in 2027. The announcement was published by IBM Newsroom and reported by The Quantum Insider on the same day. The r3 processor is a design target rather than hardware in service: IBM states that the chip "will be built to" the specification announced, and the 1,040-qubit system is a plan for 2027, not a machine that exists today.

The announcement places IBM on a path beyond 1,000 qubits, a scale the company presents as a step toward quantum computers capable of work that is impractical for classical machines. The claim rests on two elements: a larger processor, and a modular method for connecting processors together so that their qubit counts can be combined.

## The Nighthawk r3 processor

The Nighthawk r3 is designed with 520 programmable qubits out of 2,034 total physical qubits on the chip, according to IBM. The processor is designed to execute 10,000 quantum operations, a figure IBM presents as a measure of the depth of computation the chip is intended to sustain. The chip also carries 10 chip-to-chip connectors, known as l-couplers, which are the components that allow two processors to be joined into one larger system.

The distinction between programmable qubits and total physical qubits matters. The 520 programmable qubits are the qubits available for computation. The remaining physical qubits support error management and control functions. A headline qubit count therefore describes only part of the chip, and the number of operations a processor can execute before errors accumulate is a separate and equally important measure.

## Modularity: linking processors together

The central technical claim in the announcement is modularity. Rather than building a single ever-larger chip, IBM plans to connect smaller processors into a larger system. The company reports that it has already linked two Nighthawk r1 processors using four l-couplers, achieving 99.3 percent state-transfer fidelity between the chips. The stated target for this link is 99.9 percent fidelity.

IBM also reports that it has linked two cryogenic modules, the refrigeration units that cool quantum processors to operating temperature, and that the combined system was cooled below 15 millikelvin. Cooling to this level is required because quantum processors operate only at temperatures close to absolute zero. The ability to connect cryogenic modules is a precondition for systems that contain more than one processor, since each additional chip adds heat and control wiring that a single module cannot accommodate.

The 2027 plan follows directly from this work. Two r3 processors, each with 520 programmable qubits, would be linked through their l-couplers to form a single system with 1,040 programmable qubits. IBM has not stated a date within 2027 for this step, and the r3 processor itself has not yet been built.

## The current hardware: Nighthawk r2

The processor in service today is the Nighthawk r2, which carries 120 programmable qubits and has been in service since September 2026. According to IBM, the r2 has run 34 billion circuits since it entered service. The company also reports speedups of up to 19 times on partner workloads when compared with its previous generation of processors, the Heron family. The energy company E.ON reported a speedup of 15 times, and a joint IBM and Oak Ridge National Laboratory workload reported a speedup of 12 times.

These figures require careful reading. They are partner-reported results measured against IBM's own previous processors, not independent benchmarks against competing quantum hardware or against classical computers. They show that the r2 performs substantially better than its predecessor on the workloads tested, but they do not establish a general performance advantage over all alternatives.

## What IBM said

Jay Gambetta, Director of IBM Research, described the standard by which the company judges its progress. "Useful quantum computing hinges on whether results can be delivered with accuracy and speed, both are fundamental." The statement frames the announcement as a claim about quality as well as scale: a larger qubit count is useful only if the system returns correct results quickly enough to matter.

The emphasis on accuracy connects to the fidelity figures reported for the processor links. A connection between two chips that loses information at each transfer would cancel the benefit of adding qubits. The reported 99.3 percent state-transfer fidelity, against a target of 99.9 percent, shows both the progress made and the distance remaining.

## Why it matters

If the plan holds, the 1,040-qubit system would be the largest quantum system IBM has assembled, and one of the largest announced by any company. The modular approach matters because it offers a route past the physical limits of a single chip. Fabricating ever-larger monolithic processors runs into limits of yield, wiring density and cooling. Linking smaller, proven processors together is a way to keep scaling without solving all of those problems at once.

The approach also matters for the economics of quantum computing. A modular design allows a manufacturer to reuse a proven processor design and to repair or replace individual modules, rather than discarding an entire large chip when one part fails. Whether this advantage materialises in practice will depend on the fidelity of the links at scale, which is the figure IBM is still working to improve.

## What happens next

The next verifiable step is the construction of the r3 processor itself, followed by the linking of two r3 chips in 2027. Until the r3 is built and tested, the 520-qubit figure and the 10,000-operation figure remain design specifications rather than measured results. The 1,040-qubit system is likewise a stated plan, and its realisation will depend on the r3 meeting its specification and on the l-coupler links reaching the fidelity IBM targets.

Observers should watch for three specific results: first, confirmation that the r3 has been fabricated and is operating; second, measured fidelity figures for links between r3 processors; third, performance figures from partners on workloads run on the larger system, with the comparison hardware stated explicitly. Each of these would convert a part of the announcement from a plan into a measured fact.

## Caveats and limits

Three qualifications apply to this announcement. First, the r3 processor is a design target. IBM uses the language "will be built to" for its specifications, which means the figures describe intent, not measured hardware. Second, the 1,040-qubit figure is a 2027 plan for two linked chips, not a single chip and not a system in service today. Third, the speedup figures of up to 19 times are partner-reported results measured against IBM's previous Heron processors, not independent benchmarks, and they apply to specific workloads rather than to quantum computing in general.

Source: IBM Newsroom, 11 November 2026; The Quantum Insider, 11 November 2026.

title: Vivo confirms X500 series India launch on November 26
body:
Vivo confirmed on 12 November 2026 that the X500 series will launch in India on 26 November 2026 at 12:00 PM IST. The announcement was issued by Vivo India on X and published on the company's official India website. The launch covers all three models in the series — the X500, the X500 Pro and the X500 Pro Max — and will also include the Vivo Watch GT2 and a set of imaging accessories.

The confirmation resolves a question that had remained open until today. The X500 Pro Max had already been confirmed for the Indian market. The 12 November announcement adds the standard X500 and the X500 Pro to the launch, so the full series will be presented at a single event. The announcement was reported on 12 November by GSMArena, 91mobiles, Gadgets360 and Business Today, and by GizmoChina.

## What launches on 26 November

The event will introduce the three handsets, the Vivo Watch GT2, the X500 Pro Max Photographer Kit and the Vivo Imaging Grip Kit. Two telephoto extenders will also be offered in India. The 200 mm ZEISS Telephoto Extender Gen 2 is compatible with all three models, while the 400 mm ZEISS Telephoto Extender Gen 2 Ultra is compatible with the Pro Max only. Both extenders are sold separately.

The Vivo Watch GT2 will launch at the same event. According to Vivo's advertising in India, the watch offers battery life of up to 25 days, and it carries a 2.07-inch display. The company has not published a price for the watch, and the 25-day figure is a manufacturer claim rather than an independently measured result.

## The three models

The three models differ in chipset and battery capacity. The standard X500 uses the MediaTek Dimensity 9600M. The X500 Pro and the X500 Pro Max use the Dimensity 9600 Pro, a 2 nm chipset manufactured by TSMC. The distinction places the Pro models on the newer silicon, while the standard model uses a related but separate part.

Battery capacities for the Indian models are stated by Vivo as typical values on the company's India website. The X500 carries a 7,500 mAh battery, the X500 Pro a 6,510 mAh battery, and the X500 Pro Max a 7,800 mAh battery. The 8,000 mAh figure that appears in some coverage describes the China variant of the Pro Max and does not apply to the Indian model. The difference is material: the Indian Pro Max carries 200 mAh less than the China variant.

All three models support 90 W wired charging and 40 W wireless charging. Vivo has not published charging times for the Indian models, so the time required for a full charge remains unconfirmed.

## Cameras and the ZEISS system

Imaging is the central differentiator of the series, and the ZEISS partnership remains central to it. The X500 and the X500 Pro both carry a 64 MP ZEISS APO periscope telephoto camera. The X500 offers 3.1x optical zoom, while the X500 Pro offers 3.5x optical zoom at an 85 mm equivalent focal length.

The X500 Pro Max carries a 200 MP ZEISS APO telephoto camera built on the Samsung HP0 sensor, also at 3.5x optical zoom. The Pro and the Pro Max additionally carry a 50 MP ZEISS TrueDynamic main camera and a 50 MP ultra-wide camera. The telephoto extenders announced alongside the phones extend this system further, with the 400 mm extender reserved for the Pro Max.

## A new finish for the standard X500

The standard X500 will be offered in a new red finish that has not been seen on the series before. The red model carries a smaller circular camera module with a separate flash, a design detail that distinguishes it from the other finishes. The red finish is not offered in China, and it is not on sale in Europe or Southeast Asia. It therefore appears to be a finish prepared specifically for the Indian market, although Vivo has not stated that explicitly.

## What remains unannounced

Indian pricing, memory configurations and the sale date have not been announced. Unconfirmed reports from tipsters place the starting prices at ₹1,19,999 for the X500, ₹1,49,999 for the X500 Pro and ₹1,79,999 for the Pro Max, with sales reported to begin on 2 December. These figures are not confirmed by Vivo and should be treated as unconfirmed until the company states them. No official statement on pricing or availability has been issued as of 12 November.

## Why it matters

The launch matters for three reasons. First, Vivo is bringing the complete series to India in a single event, including the Pro Max that had already been confirmed and the two models confirmed only today. A complete launch gives buyers a choice across the range at the outset, rather than a staggered release.

Second, the series is built around telephoto imaging to a degree that is unusual for a mainstream flagship line. A 200 MP periscope telephoto camera, a 400 mm extender and a dedicated Photographer Kit together position the Pro Max as a device aimed at buyers who treat the phone as a camera. The ZEISS branding on the optics and on the extenders shows that the partnership extends beyond the phone body into accessories.

Third, the battery figures are large for flagship devices. A 7,800 mAh battery in the Pro Max and a 7,500 mAh battery in the standard model exceed the capacities commonly found in premium handsets. The trade-off is visible in the Pro, which carries the smallest battery of the three at 6,510 mAh despite its higher position in the range, a difference that Vivo has not explained.

## What happens next

The launch event takes place on 26 November 2026 at 12:00 PM IST. Pricing, memory configurations, the sale date and the price of the Watch GT2 are expected to be disclosed at the event. Until then, the confirmed facts are the date, the three models, the accessories, the chipsets, the battery capacities and the camera specifications stated above. Any price quoted before the event is unconfirmed.

Source: Vivo India (@Vivo_India) on X; Vivo India official website; GSMArena; 91mobiles; Gadgets360; Business Today; GizmoChina.

title: Microsoft's Lazarus: 7 edited neurons turn an AI agent into a sleeper backdoor
body:
Microsoft Research disclosed on 10 November 2026 a method by which a small number of edits to a trained language model can turn an AI agent into a sleeper backdoor. The technique, named Lazarus, rewrites fewer than 10 rarely firing neurons in the final feed-forward layer of a model, with no retraining and no poisoned training data. The disclosure is a research finding, not a report of an attack observed in the wild. Microsoft Threat Intelligence stated that it has not observed any threat actors weaponizing this technique.

The paper, titled "Lazare, veni foras: Reprogramming Dormant Neurons to Backdoor AI Agents", was published by Microsoft Research together with the Microsoft AI Red Team. Its authors are Yuchen Zeng, Giorgio Severi, Blake Bullwinkel, Eric Horvitz and Dimitris Papailiopoulos. The findings were reported by CSO Online and InfoWorld, with a further note from CSA Labs, all drawing on the Microsoft Research blog post of 10 November 2026.

## The technique

Lazarus targets neurons that fire only rarely during normal use, described in the paper as dormant neurons. The edit is applied to the final feed-forward layer of the model, a SwiGLU layer, and rewrites the behaviour of a handful of those neurons so that they respond to a chosen trigger. The procedure uses inference compute only. It does not require the model to be retrained, and it does not require any poisoned data to be inserted into the training set.

The attack is not a remote exploit. It requires write access to the model checkpoint, the stored file that contains the trained weights. An attacker would need to obtain that access through a compromised account, a compromised pipeline, or compromised storage. Without checkpoint access, the technique cannot be applied.

## The numbers

The strongest result was obtained on Nemotron-Terminal-8B, a model from NVIDIA. Editing 7 of the model's more than 12,000 neurons caused the payload to execute in at least 98.8 percent of held-out triggered sessions, and in 0 percent of benign sessions. The edit was fitted on 23 trajectories, and the success rate rose to 99.7 percent when 2,405 samples were used.

The same approach was demonstrated on two further models, with lower success rates. On Qwen3.6-27B, editing 6 neurons produced a 51.0 percent success rate when fitted on 23 samples, rising to 83.7 percent with 2,393 samples. The method was also shown to work on Gemma-4-31B-IT. The 98.8 percent figure therefore describes the Nemotron result only. Across the models tested, reported success rates ranged from 51 percent to 99.5 percent, and the figure falls sharply when the edit is fitted on few samples.

## How the trigger works

The backdoor remains inactive until a chosen condition appears in the model's context. One trigger demonstrated in the paper is a date: the clock passing midnight into 2027, on 1 January 2027. A trigger can also be an ordinary string appearing in tool output or in surrounding context, which makes it difficult to distinguish from legitimate input.

Until the trigger fires, the backdoored model passes normal evaluations. It behaves as the unmodified model would, and standard testing does not reveal the edit. When the trigger appears, the agent executes the attacker's command using the permissions it already holds. In the published tests, the payload was a harmless marker command, chosen to demonstrate the mechanism without causing damage. The tests do not show a malicious payload being executed.

## Discovery and detection

The core idea behind Lazarus was discovered autonomously by Claude Code running Opus 4.5 in February 2026, according to the Microsoft Research account. The discovery was made by an AI system working on the problem, and the method was then developed and tested by the Microsoft research team.

Microsoft also reported work on detection. Agent-built detectors flagged 91.4 percent of edited checkpoints at a 9.7 percent false-positive rate, without requiring a reference model for comparison. The result shows that detection is possible but imperfect: roughly one in eleven edited checkpoints would pass undetected, and roughly one in ten clean checkpoints would be flagged incorrectly. Microsoft stated that no scan can prove beyond any doubt that a model is safe, and the paper presents detection as an open problem rather than a solved one.

## Why it matters

The finding matters because AI agents increasingly hold real permissions. An agent deployed in a workplace may have access to files, tools, messaging systems and application programming interfaces. A backdoor that survives evaluation and activates only on a specific date or string would allow an attacker to wait for a moment of their choosing before issuing a command, with the agent's existing authority behind it.

The risk is concentrated in the supply chain for model checkpoints. Organisations that download, fine-tune or host models are trusting that the checkpoint they received is the checkpoint the publisher produced. Lazarus shows that a small, targeted edit to that file can create a persistent backdoor that normal testing will not catch. The integrity of model storage and distribution therefore becomes a security boundary in its own right, comparable to the integrity of software binaries.

## What happens next

Microsoft disclosed the method so that defenders can study it and build detection for it. The paper provides the evidence base for that work, including the success rates across models and the detection results reported above. Further research will be needed to reduce the false-positive rate of detectors and to close the remaining gap in coverage.

For organisations that run AI agents, the practical consequence is immediate and narrow. Checkpoint provenance should be verified, access to model storage should be treated as privileged, and evaluation alone should not be taken as proof that a model is clean. The technique has not been observed in use by any threat actor, and the disclosure is intended to keep it that way.

Source: Microsoft Research blog, 10 November 2026; CSO Online; InfoWorld; CSA Labs note.

title: OpenAI brings GPT-6 Luna processing to India
body:
OpenAI announced on 12 November 2026 that application programming interface (API) processing for eligible businesses and developers in India will now take place inside the country. The change applies at launch to GPT-6 Luna, the company's current flagship model, accessed through the Responses and Chat Completions APIs. Both request processing and model computation now occur in India, and supported customer content is stored in the country. The announcement was reported by The Economic Times, The Times of India, The Hindu BusinessLine, PTI via Rediff, and Express Computer, all quoting an OpenAI company statement. No standalone OpenAI blog post on the announcement was located at the time of reporting, and the account below rests on that company statement as carried by the five outlets.

The move extends OpenAI's existing data residency arrangements in India. Until now, the company's India residency offering covered the storage of customer data. The 12 November announcement adds inference, the stage at which a model receives a prompt and generates a response, to the in-country scope. For eligible customers, the full cycle of an API request, from receipt through computation to the return of a result, now remains within Indian infrastructure.

## What OpenAI announced

Under the new arrangement, eligible businesses and developers in India can run GPT-6 Luna workloads through the Responses and Chat Completions APIs with processing and computation located in India. Supported customer content is stored in the country as part of the same arrangement. The change is described by the company as live at launch for eligible customers, who can begin by creating a new API project, selecting India for storage and processing, and using the India regional endpoint.

The announcement forms part of the "OpenAI for India" initiative, the company's programme of India-focused activity, which includes a data-centre partnership with the Tata Group. The reports do not specify the number, locations or capacity of the data centres involved, and OpenAI did not disclose an investment figure.

## From storage to full inference

The distinction between storage residency and inference residency is central to the announcement. Data residency, as previously offered in India, meant that customer content was stored on servers located in the country. Inference residency goes further: the computation itself, the model run that turns a prompt into an output, is also performed in the country. The request therefore does not leave Indian infrastructure at any stage, according to the company statement.

India becomes the third market in which OpenAI offers inference residency, joining Australia and Japan. The three markets share the same conditions. Regional processing in each of them requires Zero Data Retention to be enabled and Standard pay-as-you-go processing to be used, and hosted tools are not currently available for regional processing in any of the three markets. These conditions were stated by the company and reported across the outlets covering the announcement.

## How eligible customers start

Access is limited to eligible businesses and developers, and to supported workloads. A customer begins by creating a new API project, selecting India for both storage and processing, and directing requests to the India regional endpoint. The reports do not specify the eligibility criteria in detail, and it is not clear from the published accounts whether all existing Indian API customers qualify automatically or whether eligibility is assessed case by case.

The scope of the launch is narrow in one further respect. At launch, the in-country processing applies to GPT-6 Luna only. Other OpenAI models were not named in the announcement as part of the India processing capability. The company did not state a timetable for extending regional processing to additional models.

## The conditions and limits

Three conditions define the practical scope of the announcement. First, regional processing requires Zero Data Retention to be enabled, the setting under which the company does not retain API request and response data. Second, it requires Standard pay-as-you-go processing. Third, hosted tools, the company-provided tools that can be invoked during an API call, are not currently available for regional processing in India, Australia or Japan.
